segments.text: Light can be trapped. Glass fibres carry it under oceans, and photonic chips route it through wires half a micron wide.
segments.say: Light can be trapped. Glass fibres carry it under oceans, and photonic chips route it through wires, half a micron wide.

segments.text: This ring, a few microns across, sorts colours. Send in several, and most pass straight by…
segments.say: This ring, a few microns across, sorts colours. Send in several, and most pass straight by.

segments.text: …but one colour drops into the ring, circles it, and leaves through the other wire.
segments.say: But one colour drops into the ring, circles it, and leaves through the other wire.

segments.text: How do you trap light in a wire? And why do only certain colours fit?
segments.say: How do you trap light in a wire? And why do only certain colours fit?

segments.text: Start with a strip of glass, the core, surrounded by material of lower refractive index, the cladding.
segments.say: Start with a strip of glass, the core, surrounded by material of lower refractive index: the cladding.

segments.text: A ray that meets the wall at a shallow angle can't escape. It's totally reflected, and zigzags along the core.
segments.say: A ray that meets the wall at a shallow angle can't escape. It's totally reflected, and zigzags along the core.

segments.text: But light is a wave. The zigzag is really two plane waves crossing: one heading up, one heading down.
segments.say: But light is a wave. The zigzag is really two plane waves crossing: one heading up, and one heading down.

segments.text: Together they form a standing wave across the core, which travels along it.
segments.say: Together, they form a standing wave across the core, which travels along it.

segments.text: But not every angle works. Follow the wave up across the core and back: it must return in step with itself, or the bounces cancel.
segments.say: But not every angle works. Follow the wave up across the core and back. It must return in step with itself, or the bounces cancel.

segments.text: So the round-trip phase must be a whole number of turns, 2πm. Slide the angle, and only a few angles click into place.
segments.say: So the round trip phase must be a whole number of turns: two pi em. Slide the angle, and only a few angles click into place.

segments.text: These are the modes. Each keeps its shape as it travels, with tails that fade into the cladding: evanescent waves.
segments.say: These are the modes. Each keeps its shape as it travels, with tails that fade into the cladding: evanescent waves.

segments.text: There's a cleaner way to find modes, with linear algebra.
segments.say: There's a cleaner way to find modes, with linear algebra.

segments.text: A mode is a shape E(x) that travels as e^(iβz). Put that into the wave equation, and out comes an eigenvalue problem.
segments.say: A mode is a shape, E of ex, that travels as, e to the i beta zee. Put that into the wave equation, and out comes an eigenvalue problem.

segments.text: Sample x on a grid. The second derivative becomes a tridiagonal matrix, and the index profile adds to its diagonal.
segments.say: Sample ex on a grid. The second derivative becomes a tri-diagonal matrix, and the index profile adds to its diagonal.

segments.text: Its eigenvectors are the mode shapes. Its eigenvalues give each mode's propagation constant, β.
segments.say: Its eigenvectors are the mode shapes. Its eigenvalues give each mode's propagation constant, beta.

segments.text: And each effective index, β/k₀, lies between the cladding and core indices.
segments.say: And each effective index, beta over kay zero, lies between the cladding and core indices.

segments.text: Any input is a sum of modes, each advancing its own phase. It's the angular spectrum method from episode one, with modes in place of plane waves.
segments.say: Any input is a sum of modes, each advancing its own phase. It's the angular spectrum method from episode one, with modes in place of plane waves.

segments.text: Launch an off-centre spot into a wide guide. The modes beat into a kaleidoscope, then fall back in step, and the spot reappears.
segments.say: Launch an off-centre spot into a wide guide. The modes beat into a kaleidoscope, then fall back in step, and the spot reappears.

segments.text: Now place two identical guides side by side, so close that their tails overlap, and launch light into one.
segments.say: Now place two identical guides side by side, so close that their tails overlap, and launch light into one.

segments.text: It drifts across into the other guide, then comes back, again and again.
segments.say: It drifts across into the other guide, then comes back, again and again.

segments.text: Why? The pair has modes of its own: one symmetric, one antisymmetric, with propagation constants β + κ and β − κ.
segments.say: Why? The pair has modes of its own: one symmetric, one antisymmetric, with propagation constants beta plus kappa, and beta minus kappa.

segments.text: Light in one guide is the sum of the two. One slowly falls behind, and after a distance π/2κ it has flipped sign: now the sum sits in the other guide.
segments.say: Light in one guide is the sum of the two. One slowly falls behind, and after a distance, pi over two kappa, it has flipped sign. Now the sum sits in the other guide.

segments.text: In the basis of the two guides, that's a 2×2 rotation: amplitude cos κz in one, i sin κz in the other.
segments.say: In the basis of the two guides, that's a two by two rotation: amplitude cosine kappa zee in one, and i sine kappa zee in the other.

segments.text: Stop halfway and you have a 50:50 splitter, the building block of interferometers, switches and optical processors.
segments.say: Stop halfway, and you have a fifty-fifty splitter: the building block of interferometers, switches, and optical processors.

segments.text: To store light, bend a guide into a ring beside a straight one. On every pass, a little light leaks across into the ring.
segments.say: To store light, bend a guide into a ring, beside a straight one. On every pass, a little light leaks across into the ring.

segments.text: Each round trip adds another copy, rotated by the round-trip phase, and a little weaker than the last.
segments.say: Each round trip adds another copy, rotated by the round trip phase, and a little weaker than the last.

segments.text: Off resonance, the copies curl into a small spiral, and mostly cancel.
segments.say: Off resonance, the copies curl into a small spiral, and mostly cancel.

segments.text: On resonance, when the ring fits a whole number of wavelengths, they line up into one long arrow. The light piles up.
segments.say: On resonance, when the ring fits a whole number of wavelengths, they line up into one long arrow. The light piles up.

segments.text: Sweep the colour, and the stored light spikes at evenly spaced resonances. That's what the ring in the opening did.
segments.say: Sweep the colour, and the stored light spikes at evenly spaced resonances. That's what the ring in the opening did.

segments.text: How sharp is each spike? That's set by loss: the more round trips the light survives, the narrower the peak.
segments.say: How sharp is each spike? That's set by loss. The more round trips the light survives, the narrower the peak.

segments.text: We measure it with the quality factor: the wavelength over the peak's width, Q = λ/Δλ. High Q means light stays stored for a long time.
segments.say: We measure it with the quality factor: the wavelength over the peak's width, Q equals lambda over delta lambda. A high Q means light stays stored for a long time.

segments.text: Now watch the light that goes straight past. It meets the light leaking back out of the ring, which on resonance comes out flipped.
segments.say: Now watch the light that goes straight past. It meets the light leaking back out of the ring, which, on resonance, comes out flipped.

segments.text: So the through port dims. When the ring leaks out exactly as fast as it loses light inside, the two cancel completely: critical coupling.
segments.say: So the through port dims. When the ring leaks out exactly as fast as it loses light inside, the two cancel completely: critical coupling.

segments.text: Couple more weakly, or more strongly, and the dip gets shallower.
segments.say: Couple more weakly, or more strongly, and the dip gets shallower.

segments.text: On a computer, each idea takes just a few lines.
segments.say: On a computer, each idea takes just a few lines.

segments.text: Modes: build the tridiagonal matrix and call an eigenvalue solver. Make the window wide enough for the tails, or its edges squeeze the modes.
segments.say: Modes: build the tri-diagonal matrix, and call an eigenvalue solver. Make the window wide enough for the tails, or its edges squeeze the modes.

segments.text: Propagation: the beam propagation method, BPM. It alternates two steps: diffraction, an FFT as in episode one, and refraction, a thin phase screen.
segments.say: Propagation: the beam propagation method, B P M. It alternates two steps: diffraction, an F F T, as in episode one. And refraction: a thin phase screen.

segments.text: Repeat, slice after slice. That's how the coupler was computed.
segments.say: Repeat, slice after slice. That's how the coupler was computed.

segments.text: Resonators: add up the round trips, a geometric series, in one line.
segments.say: Resonators: add up the round trips, a geometric series, in one line.

segments.text: The catch: BPM only marches forward, at gentle angles. Fine for couplers, but wrong for tight bends and reflections.
segments.say: The catch: B P M only marches forward, at gentle angles. Fine for couplers, but wrong for tight bends, and reflections.

segments.text: Trapped light settles into modes, the eigenvectors of the cross-section. A resonator stores light where round trips add in phase.
segments.say: Trapped light settles into modes, the eigenvectors of the cross section. A resonator stores light where round trips add in phase.

segments.text: But these shortcuts assume gentle, forward-going light. Sharp bends, gratings and nanostructures break that, and then you need Maxwell's equations themselves.
segments.say: But these shortcuts assume gentle, forward going light. Sharp bends, gratings, and nanostructures break that, and then you need Maxwell's equations themselves.

segments.text: How does a computer solve them? Next time.
segments.say: How does a computer solve them? Next time.
